description:
Division: Leadership & Operations
Location: Oregon; statewide travel required
Reports to: Vice President of Operations
Employment Type: Full-Time, Exempt

About Golden Grail Group

Golden Grail Group is a vertically integrated cannabis company with operations across Oregon and Washington. Our business spans retail, cultivation, product processing and production, and wholesale. Our portfolio includes retail brands such as Chalice, Homegrown Oregon, Local Leaf, The Herb Center, and Dr. Jolly’s, alongside farm, product, and wholesale brands. Across Oregon’s regulated producer, processor, wholesaler, and retailer activities, our teams bring products from cultivation and manufacturing through distribution and into retail.

The Opportunity

Golden Grail Group is seeking a skilled, people-centered Director of Operations to lead teams and facilities across Oregon. This is an opportunity to strengthen leadership capability, operating consistency, and collaboration across a complex, multi-site business while supporting the company’s growth and scaling initiatives.

The Director will oversee extraction, production, warehousing, distribution, logistics, and related operations. Success in this role depends on building capable leaders and accountable teams, improving how work moves across facilities, and balancing business performance with a strong employee experience. The Director partners closely with Human Resources, Finance, Retail, Sales, and Compliance on workforce planning, employee development, performance, budgets, and company-wide initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

People Leadership, Culture & Team Development

  • Lead, motivate, and develop facility managers, department leaders, and operational teams across Oregon.
  • Build a people-first culture grounded in trust, accountability, respect, clear communication, and shared ownership of results.
  • Maintain a visible, approachable leadership presence so employees feel informed, supported, and connected to company priorities.
  • Set clear expectations, provide constructive feedback, recognize strong performance, and address performance or conduct concerns consistently and respectfully.
  • Coach managers in communication, conflict resolution, decision-making, delegation, employee engagement, and day-to-day leadership.
  • Establish consistent leadership meetings, site visits, one-on-ones, performance check-ins, and follow-through on commitments.
  • Develop leadership capability and succession depth through coaching, mentoring, cross-training, and development planning.
  • Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, recruiting, onboarding, training, employee relations, performance management, retention, and organizational change.
  • Assess staffing, morale, communication, and team effectiveness across locations and implement practical solutions with site leaders and Human Resources.

Regional & Multi-Site Operational Leadership

  • Provide strategic and day-to-day leadership across cultivation, extraction, production, warehousing, distribution, logistics, and related operations.
  • Translate company strategy and scaling initiatives into regional operating plans, staffing priorities, performance expectations, and measurable outcomes.
  • Maintain regular on-site presence, assess operational and team performance, and ensure leaders have the resources and support needed to succeed.
  • Establish consistent regional standards while accounting for differences in capacity, staffing, product flow, and local operating needs.
  • Promote collaboration across locations and functions, reduce silos, and serve as the regional escalation point for significant operational and people concerns.
  • Monitor regional priorities and performance indicators, holding leaders accountable for timely execution and sustainable results.
  • Support the evaluation and integration of new initiatives, facilities, processes, and organizational changes as business needs evolve.

Production, Supply Chain & Facilities

  • Oversee cultivation, extraction, manufacturing, and production workflows, including capacity planning, scheduling, quality standards, equipment utilization, and finished-goods delivery.
  • Direct warehouse, inventory, distribution, transportation, and logistics activities to support reliable product movement.
  • Partner with Retail and Sales leaders to align production and distribution priorities with demand, promotions, product launches, and inventory needs.
  • Identify operational constraints and engage teams in solutions that improve service, quality, employee experience, and cost control.
  • Maintain business-continuity plans and provide steady leadership during staffing, equipment, vendor, facility, or supply-chain challenges.

Compliance, Safety & Quality

  • Ensure assigned locations operate in accordance with Oregon cannabis regulations, OLCC requirements, Metrc procedures, safety standards, and internal policies.
  • Reinforce team ownership of compliance, safety, and quality through training, coaching, communication, and accountability.
  • Maintain controls for inventory movement, chain of custody, waste, product handling, documentation, access, and reconciliation.
  • Partner with Compliance, Human Resources, and site leaders on inspections, investigations, corrective actions, and incident follow-up.

Financial Management & Business Partnership

  • Partner with Finance and Human Resources on budgets, forecasts, labor models, staffing plans, capital needs, and cost-management priorities.
  • Monitor operational, financial, and workforce performance; explain material variances and implement appropriate corrective action.
  • Use data to guide staffing, resource allocation, capacity decisions, vendor strategy, and improvement priorities.
  • Provide executive leadership with clear updates regarding regional performance, risks, needs, and recommendations.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Operations, Supply Chain, Business Administration, Manufacturing, Organizational Leadership, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Eight or more years of progressive operations experience, including responsibility for multiple locations or geographically dispersed teams.
  • Five or more years of people-management experience, including direct supervision and development of managers or senior leaders.
  • Professional experience in the regulated cannabis industry, with an understanding of the operational demands of a licensed business.
  • Demonstrated ability to build engaged teams, coach leaders, manage performance, and lead through growth or change.
  • Experience leading manufacturing, production, warehousing, distribution, logistics, facilities, or other inventory-intensive operations.
  • Proven ability to establish standards, use performance metrics, manage competing priorities, and improve processes across locations.
  • Strong judgment, emotional intelligence, communication, accountability, and discretion in a fast-paced, regulated environment.
  • Ability to travel regularly throughout Oregon and respond to time-sensitive operational and people needs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a vertically integrated cannabis organization, with exposure to multiple functions such as cultivation, manufacturing, extraction, production, and distribution.
  • Working knowledge of OLCC requirements and Metrc workflows.
  • Experience overseeing multiple functions in a business that includes both wholesale and retail operations.
  • Background in consumer packaged goods, food and beverage, manufacturing, agriculture, retail supply chain, or another regulated industry.
  • Experience leading integrations, facility launches, expansions, reorganizations, or significant process improvements.

Confidentiality Expectations

This role has access to sensitive operational, financial, personnel, compensation, security, inventory, vendor, and strategic information. The Director of Operations must maintain confidentiality, exercise sound discretion, and handle sensitive information in accordance with company policy and applicable law.

This description outlines the general nature and level of the role and is not an exhaustive list of all duties or qualifications. Responsibilities may change based on business needs.

title: Manager, Engineering (Product)
description:
Company Overview

Flock Freight is the largest Shared Truckload (STL) freight brokerage in the U.S., transforming underutilized truckload capacity into tangible value: cost savings for shippers, increased earnings for carriers, and a smaller carbon footprint.

Their AI-powered, patented pooling technology optimizes across Flock’s entire customer network, combining shipments from thousands of businesses into efficient Shared Truckloads. With STL, shippers enjoy truckload-level service while only paying for the space they need. Trusted by thousands of customers, from some of the largest enterprises to growing brands, Flock Freight delivers an unmatched combination of cost efficiency, exceptional service, and a streamlined shipping experience.


Flock Freight has been a Certified B Corp since 2020, meeting high social, environmental, transparency, and accountability standards to all of our stakeholders.

Team/Department Overview: Product Engineering Team – Reporting to the Senior Manager of Product Engineering.

Flock Freight is hiring an Engineering Manager to lead a Product Engineering team responsible for the shipper and carrier applications and core workflows that power the freight experience. You will lead an established team of seven engineers, including five Staff Engineers, overseeing end-to-end delivery while providing the technical guidance needed to navigate complex engineering decisions.

This is a people-leadership role first, with a strong emphasis on coaching, developing, and empowering an experienced engineering team. You’ll foster collaboration, elevate team performance, and partner with Product, Design, Operations, and Engineering leadership to deliver reliable software that shippers, carriers, and Flock teams depend on every day.

While you won't be writing production code every day, you'll remain actively involved in architectural discussions, technical decision-making, and engineering execution. You'll work alongside experienced engineers to evaluate tradeoffs, remove obstacles, and ensure the team delivers scalable, maintainable solutions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and develop an established team of seven engineers, including Staff-level technical leaders, through meaningful coaching, regular 1:1s, constructive feedback, performance management, and individualized career development.
  • Own engineering execution and delivery, partnering with Product to translate business priorities into achievable milestones, navigate changing requirements, manage competing priorities, and consistently deliver meaningful customer and business outcomes.
  • Partner with Product, Design, and Operations to translate customer and business goals into a clear technical roadmap.
  • Provide technical leadership by guiding architectural discussions, challenging assumptions, and helping experienced engineers navigate decisions involving infrastructure, system design, scalability, and long-term maintainability.
  • Keep production healthy by establishing strong ownership, on-call practices, incident response, observability, and follow-through on corrective actions.
  • Identify opportunities to improve engineering effectiveness, developer productivity, and software quality through thoughtful improvements to testing, CI/CD, documentation, collaboration, and emerging development tools.
  • Support hiring and onboarding as the team evolves, helping attract strong engineering talent while prioritizing the development and effectiveness of the existing team.
  • Address team conflict, collaboration challenges, and performance concerns directly, fairly, and early, creating clarity around expectations and supporting people toward successful outcomes..
  • Balance new product work against technical debt and reliability investments, making tradeoffs visible to stakeholders.
  • Define and track meaningful measures of team success, including delivery predictability, product quality, operational health, team effectiveness, and business impact. Use these measures to identify risks, guide improvements, and communicate progress.
  • Communicate clearly up, down, and across the organization so the team understands its goals, priorities, tradeoffs, decisions, and the customer and business outcomes behind the work.
  • Partner with fellow engineering leaders to strengthen Flock’s engineering culture, operating practices, and technical standards, creating greater consistency and effectiveness across teams.

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with strong senior-level technical expertise or equivalent technical leadership experience.
  • 1–2 + years of demonstrated people leadership experience, whether through formal engineering management or meaningful responsibility for coaching, mentoring, developing engineers, and contributing to team performance.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • A genuine passion for developing engineers at different career stages, including experienced technical contributors, and creating an environment where collaboration, accountability, and continuous learning thrive.
  • Proven ability to navigate team conflict, resolve challenges constructively, and implement lasting process improvements.
  • Strong project-management skills: defining MVPs with Product, decomposing work into iterative deliverables, running an effective agile or iterative process, and keeping delivery on track.
  • Strong technical grounding in backend and web application development, with experience in modern technologies and frameworks. Flock’s Product Engineering stack currently emphasizes Java, Spring, Typescript and React.
  • Strong technical judgment and the ability to guide architectural decisions, challenge technical assumptions, and mentor experienced engineers while remaining focused on people leadership rather than day-to-day coding.
  • The technical credibility to engage in code reviews, design discussions, and engineering problem-solving while providing constructive guidance to engineers across different experience levels.
  • Experience partnering with Product and non-technical stakeholders to set priorities, negotiate scope, and make decisions under uncertainty.
  • Experience hiring, training, and developing engineers at multiple levels, including designing effective onboarding.
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate team conflict, resolve challenges constructively, and drive sustainable process improvements.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical tradeoffs into clear, actionable insights for non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience thriving in smaller, agile, or rapidly evolving engineering environments where adaptability, broad technical exposure, resourcefulness, and a willingness to take ownership are essential.

Compensation

The expected range for this position is $180,000 - $205,000 per year. This reflects typical earning potential in this role based on market data and individual factors including skill sets, experience, and geographic location. In addition to salary, full-time employees are eligible for an equity package and competitive benefits that support you and your family as part of your total rewards package at Flock Freight. We target candidates local or willing to relocate to Flock Freight’s San Diego headquarters.

Life & Benefits of the Flock:

  • Hybrid Work Model: As an organization we value in-office collaboration, working cross-functionally, and winning together. Through scheduled in-office and work from home days, we are able to work more efficiently and collaboratively. (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday in-Office)
  • 401(k): We know Flock may just be a stepping stone in your epic journey, but we want to be sure you’re setting your future self up for success!
  • Medical, Dental & Vision: Generous coverage for employees and dependents. Both HMO and PPO options provided.

Our Promise To You:
Flock Freight is committed to creating an environment that’s fair and inclusive. We fill our open positions based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We value the skills of people from all backgrounds and are proud to hire, promote, and retain talent from a diverse candidate pool. Diverse perspectives are central to innovation at Flock Freight and make our team better. We're interested in your inherent abilities, not just the skills you bring from your last role - if you think you have what it takes to succeed in the role but don't check every box, please still get in touch. We'd love to start a conversation with you.

Flock Freight has zero tolerance for behavior that negatively impacts marginalized groups, including women, people of color, veterans, immigrants, people with disabilities, and members of the LGBTQIA+ community. We invite people of all identities to join the Flock!

We are targeting talent in the San Diego/Encinitas and Los Angeles area.

title: Lien Resolution Team Lead
description:
POSITION OVERVIEW

The Lien Resolution Team Lead runs the function that determines how much of every settlement actually reaches our clients. You will supervise a team of reductions and lien resolution specialists, personally handle the largest and most complex lien files, and own the metrics that measure our performance — aggregate reduction rate, net-to-client percentage, and time from settlement to disbursement.

This is a negotiation role with a management layer on top. Every dollar your team takes off a medical balance, a hospital lien, or a health plan’s subrogation claim is a dollar that goes to an injured client instead. You will set the standard for how hard those negotiations are pushed, hold the team to it, and step in personally when a provider or plan will not move.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Post-settlement medical bill and liens
  • Lead the team. Supervise, train, and evaluate a team of reductions and lien resolution specialists. Assign files, manage workload distribution, run regular file reviews, and develop the team’s negotiation skills.
  • Own the numbers. Track and report aggregate reduction percentage, dollars saved, aging, and settlement-to-disbursement turnaround. Identify where the team is leaving money on the table and fix it.
  • Negotiate the hard files. Personally handle high-balance, high-complexity, and escalated reductions where the provider or plan has refused to move at the specialist level.
  • Resolve statutory and plan liens. Direct the resolution of Medicare conditional payments and Medicare Secondary Payer obligations, Florida Medicaid (AHCA) claims under Fla. Stat. § 409.910 including the administrative challenge process, ERISA and self-funded plan reimbursement claims, TRICARE and VA claims, and hospital and provider liens under applicable county ordinances.
  • Manage letter of protection balances. Negotiate LOP balances with treating providers and maintain documentation consistent with Fla. Stat. § 768.0427 disclosure requirements.
  • Apply the collateral source framework. Analyze health insurance payments, PIP benefits, and other collateral sources under Fla. Stat. § 768.76 to establish the correct reimbursement exposure before negotiating.
  • Build provider relationships. Establish and maintain working relationships and, where appropriate, standing reduction arrangements with high-volume providers, facilities, and lien resolution vendors.
  • Partner with the attorneys. Give trial and pre-suit attorneys accurate, timely lien exposure figures so they can evaluate settlement authority and advise clients on net recovery.
  • Protect the client experience. Ensure clients understand their closing statement and that disbursement is accurate, documented, and prompt.
  • Improve the process. Standardize templates, escalation paths, and negotiation playbooks; recommend and help implement case management system and workflow improvements.
  • Maintain compliance. Ensure every file satisfies trust accounting, Florida Bar, and firm documentation requirements before funds are released.

Remote Engagement Details

  • Independent contractor remote position
  • 40-hour workweek; schedule confirmed during the interview process.
  • Reliable internet, a computer, and a quiet, professional workspace required.
  • No employee benefits or paid time off.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Minimum of four (4) years of experience in medical lien resolution, reductions, or settlement negotiation at a personal injury firm, lien resolution company, or healthcare recovery vendor.
  • Minimum of 5 people managed in past roles (direct or indirect reports)
  • Demonstrated track record of negotiating meaningful reductions on medical balances and liens, with the numbers to support it.
  • Working knowledge of Medicare Secondary Payer rules and conditional payment resolution.
  • Working knowledge of Florida Medicaid third-party recovery and the AHCA lien process.
  • Familiarity with ERISA plan reimbursement claims and the practical difference between self-funded and fully insured plans.
  • Understanding of Florida PIP and the collateral source framework as it affects reimbursement exposure.
  • Strong command of settlement math — gross to net, attorney fees and costs, pro rata allocation, and common fund and made-whole considerations.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication; able to be firm with providers and plainspoken with clients.
  • Proficiency with legal case management software and spreadsheets.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish, spoken and written.
  • Paralegal certificate, or a bachelor’s degree in a related field.
  • Experience building or refining a reductions workflow from the ground up.
  • Familiarity with Medicare Set-Aside considerations in third-party liability settlements.

JOIN OUR TEAM

At The Ward Law Group, every role contributes to changing lives.

If you're looking for an opportunity to grow your litigation career, maximize client recoveries, and work alongside a high-performing legal team, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and become part of a team committed to excellence, accountability, and changing lives—one client at a time.

title: Race Systems Technician – Motorsport Communications
description:
UK Based | Extensive International Travel | Trackside Technical Support

We are working with a specialist communications business supporting leading motorsport and live event organisations worldwide.

They are looking to appoint an experienced Race Systems Technician to join their trackside support team, providing technical support across major international motorsport events.

This is a hands-on, customer-facing role combining radio communications, intercom systems, networking and real-time technical troubleshooting in demanding live environments.

The position involves extensive international travel, approximately 100 days per year, along with evening and weekend work aligned to race schedules.

The Role

The Race Systems Technician will provide both trackside and remote technical support, ensuring communication systems operate reliably throughout practice, qualifying and race sessions.

You will work directly with race teams, drivers, engineers, suppliers and event organisations, often in high-pressure environments where issues need to be resolved quickly and effectively.

Responsibilities will include:

  • Providing trackside and remote technical support for motorsport and event customers

  • Configuring and supporting two-way radio and intercom systems

  • Troubleshooting communications equipment and resolving faults in real time

  • Managing communication systems across live event environments

  • Supporting customers before, during and after events

  • Building, testing and preparing communications equipment prior to deployment

  • Managing race support equipment and maintaining accurate stock levels

  • Providing customer training on system use and basic troubleshooting

  • Maintaining clear technical documentation and resolution records

  • Supporting networking, remote access and communications infrastructure

  • Managing multiple customer requirements during busy event schedules

  • Working closely with internal technical teams to deliver reliable solutions

What We’re Looking For

  • Experience in technical support within motorsport, broadcast, AV, telecommunications or military environments

  • Strong experience with professional two-way radio systems

  • Understanding of digital radio protocols such as DMR, TETRA or similar technologies

  • Knowledge of UHF and VHF frequency management

  • Strong troubleshooting and fault-finding skills

  • Experience with radio programming, configuration and testing

  • Good soldering and electronic repair skills

  • Experience using communications test and diagnostic equipment

  • Understanding of managed networks, routing, VPNs and remote technologies

  • Strong customer service and communication skills

  • Ability to remain calm and make decisions in high-pressure live environments

  • Strong organisation and time management skills

  • Willingness to travel extensively across the UK and internationally

  • Flexibility to work evenings and weekends in line with race schedules

  • Full UK driving licence

Desirable Experience

  • Technical qualification in electronics, telecommunications or a related discipline

  • Experience with RF and spectrum management

  • Knowledge of Audio over IP technologies such as AES67 or Dante

  • Previous motorsport experience

  • Understanding of race operations and trackside environments

The Opportunity

This is an exciting opportunity for a technically strong communications professional who wants to work at the heart of international motorsport.

The role offers:

  • Competitive salary and bonus opportunities

  • Enhanced rates for out-of-hours work

  • Private healthcare

  • Extensive international travel

  • Career development and progression

  • Exposure to advanced communications technology in a fast-paced motorsport environment

If you have experience in radio communications, technical support or live event systems and would enjoy working trackside in international motorsport, we would be keen to speak with you.

On Location provides unrivaled access for corporate clients and fans looking for official, immersive experiences at marquee events, including the Olympic and Paralympic Games, FIFA World Cup 2026, Super Bowl, NCAA Final Four, and more. TKO Group Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: TKO) is a premium sports and entertainment company. TKO owns iconic properties including UFC, the world’s premier mixed martial arts organization; WWE, the global leader in sports entertainment; and PBR, the world’s premier bull riding organization. Together, these properties reach 1 billion households across 210 countries and territories and organize more than 500 live events year-round, attracting more than three million fans. TKO also services and partners with major sports rights holders through IMG, an industry-leading global sports marketing agency; and On Location, a global leader in premium experiential hospitality.



ABOUT THE ROLE

The LA28 Olympic & Paralympic Hospitality Program will deliver premium experiences across competition venues, hospitality houses, celebration spaces, and exclusive guest environments throughout the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games.


The Senior Designer, Small Format is responsible for the design and execution of small-format printed and physical guest-facing products across the LA28 Hospitality program. Working within the established LA28 Hospitality creative vision, this role translates brand and experience strategies into thoughtfully designed, production-ready pieces that support the guest journey across hospitality venues and programs. The role may also support the development and execution of select uniform and apparel applications, working in partnership with the broader creative team to ensure consistency with the Hospitality visual identity.


The role requires a highly collaborative designer with strong graphic design and typography skills, a detailed understanding of print and physical product production, and the ability to carry work from concept and design development through artwork, proofing, fabrication, delivery, and Games-time execution.


THE ROLE

Reporting to the Group Creative Director, the Senior Designer, Small Format partners with Creative, Production, Venue Development, Marketing, Operations, Interior Design, Environmental Design, Fabrication, and external agencies to develop and execute small-format design across LA28 Hospitality.


The successful candidate will design and manage a range of printed and physical products, ensuring each item is visually cohesive, functional, production-ready, and aligned with the overall hospitality experience. The role works across multiple venues, products, service levels, vendors, and production requirements while maintaining a high standard of craft and brand consistency.


CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

Small Format Design Development

  • Design small-format printed and physical products from concept through final production.

Creative Collaboration

Quality & Brand Stewardship

Innovation

SUCCESS IN THIS ROLE

title: Identity Solutions Manager
description:
Who We Are:



TKO Group Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: TKO) is a premium sports and entertainment company. TKO owns iconic properties including UFC, the world’s premier mixed martial arts organization; WWE, the global leader in sports entertainment; and PBR, the world’s premier bull riding organization. Together, these properties reach 1 billion households across 210 countries and territories and organize more than 500 live events year-round, attracting more than three million fans. TKO also services and partners with major sports rights holders through IMG, an industry-leading global sports marketing agency; and On Location, a global leader in premium experiential hospitality.



Title: Identity Solutions Manager

Location: New York, NY (Hybrid) or Stamford

Reports To: Director, Cloud & Platform Engineering

Position Summary

The Identity Solutions Manager is TKO's business-facing leader for Identity and Access Management. This is the person who makes modern identity real and relevant across UFC, WWE, IMG, PBR, OLE, and the broader portfolio. They translate complex IAM concepts into outcomes that non-technical stakeholders can appreciate, support, and act on, and they build the internal credibility that turns business teams from passive recipients of identity changes into active advocates for them.

As the primary advocate for modern identity at TKO, they will serve as the connective tissue across three layers simultaneously:

  • Capturing, prioritizing, and maintaining business requirements in a structured engineering backlog

  • Partnering with Identity Architects to shape and communicate our IAM/Okta roadmap

  • Ensuring operational readiness with Helpdesk frontline support so they are always informed and ready for what comes next.

The Identity Solutions Manager will be the spearhead of TKO’s IAM strategy, coordinating multiple Identity Automation and Lifecycle Programs, balancing competing demands, aligning stakeholders, and ensuring engineering investment is focused on TKO’s highest-value strategic initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Business Liaison & Evangelism

  • Serve as the primary business-facing liaison for Identity Engineering, conducting discovery sessions to capture requirements and translate them into actionable identity system specifications

  • Act as an internal evangelist for TKO's Okta-based IAM capabilities, educating business teams across the portfolio on what's possible and driving adoption of SSO, automated provisioning, and access governance features

  • Own business-facing roadmap communication, ensuring stakeholders understand what's coming, why it matters, and how it benefits them

  • Be the voice of the business inside Identity Engineering, advocating for requirements, influencing prioritization, and ensuring engineering effort stays aligned to business value

Intake, Backlog & Program Execution

  • Manage governance intake requests, maintain and prioritize the program backlog, and ensure Identity Engineering is consistently focused on the highest-value initiatives

  • Coordinate and drive execution of the SOX Application Lifecycle Governance Program, including application onboarding, ownership validation, access request processes, and user access reviews

  • Partner with Identity Engineering, Security, Compliance, Internal Audit, and business stakeholders to deliver governance initiatives on time and in scope

  • Proactively identify risks, dependencies, and blockers; develop mitigation plans and escalate issues before they impact delivery

Stakeholder Management & Communication

  • Facilitate stakeholder meetings, workshops, and program reviews, tailoring communication effectively for technical and non-technical audiences

  • Serve as the bridge between Identity Architects and Helpdesk teams, translating roadmap milestones into operational context so frontline teams are always prepared for what's coming

  • Drive accountability across stakeholders, ensuring commitments and action items are completed within agreed timelines

  • Develop and deliver regular status reporting, governance metrics, dashboards, and executive updates

Skills & Abilities

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Business Analysis: Runs requirements workshops, documents current and future state, and translates ambiguous business needs into actionable identity system specifications

  • Product Evangelism: Excites and educates non-technical stakeholders about Okta-based IAM capabilities, turning skeptics into advocates and driving meaningful adoption across the business

  • Stakeholder Management: Builds strong relationships across technical and business teams; influences decisions, drives alignment, and navigates competing priorities with confidence

  • Communication: Tailors written and verbal messaging effectively for executive leadership, business stakeholders, auditors, and engineering teams

Program Delivery

  • Program Execution: Develops actionable plans, manages competing priorities, and drives deliverables forward with minimal oversight in fast-paced, high-visibility environments

  • Intake & Backlog Management: Manages governance intake requests, maintains a prioritized program backlog, and ensures engineering focus stays aligned to business and compliance objectives

  • Risk Management: Proactively identifies risks, dependencies, and blockers then develops mitigation strategies and escalates before issues impact delivery

  • Documentation: Produces clear, professional status reports, governance records, meeting summaries, and executive communications

Technical Knowledge

  • IAM & Governance: Working understanding of SSO, SCIM provisioning, JIT provisioning, REST APIs, access request processes, user access reviews, and automated identity lifecycle management

  • Okta Fluency: Hands-on expertise with Okta Identity Cloud, Okta Workflows, Okta Identity Governance (OIG) is required to build enough to credibly evangelize capabilities and partner effectively with engineering

  • Technical Aptitude: Able to engage meaningfully on identity architecture, application onboarding requirements, governance controls, and integration dependencies without needing to be an engineer

Ways of Working

  • Extreme Ownership Mindset: Takes full accountability for successes and failures, proactively solves problems, removes roadblocks, and follows through with commitments until fully delivered.

  • Comfort with Ambiguity: Brings structure and clarity to evolving requirements and complex initiatives without waiting for perfect information

  • Ownership & Accountability: Takes personal responsibility for outcomes and holds stakeholders to commitments without being heavy-handed

  • Resilience: Maintains composure and focus across multiple concurrent initiatives in a dynamic, high-growth environment

Qualifications (required)

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business, or a related field or equivalent hands-on experience

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience with Okta Identity Cloud, Okta Workflows, and Okta Identity Governance

  • 7+ years of experience in a business-facing technology role, such as business analyst, technical program manager, or IAM practitioner with stakeholder-facing responsibilities

  • Demonstrated experience translating business requirements into technical specifications in an enterprise environment

  • Working knowledge of identity and access management concepts, including SSO, provisioning, user access reviews, and access governance

  • Strong organization skillsets with managing program backlog, prioritize competing demands, and drive cross-functional delivery in a complex organization

  • Experience supporting IAM programs with alignment to compliance frameworks such as SOX, PCI DSS, or NIST

KPIs for Identity Solutions Manager

Identity Program Delivery

  • Deliver on 95% of committed Identity Engineering initiatives on time, in budget, and within agreed scope

Application Lifecycle Governance Adoption

  • Successfully onboard and operationalize 100% of targeted SOX and priority business applications into TKO’s Okta Identity Governance framework

Backlog & Intake Management

  • Develop and maintain a prioritized engineering backlog with 100% of intake requests recorded and triaged within 5 business days and business priorities aligned to quarterly roadmap objectives

Executive Reporting & Governance

  • Develop and maintain executive IAM dashboards and governance reporting, delivering accurate monthly metrics on application onboarding, automation adoption, access governance, program health, risks, and roadmap progress to IT Leadership and Internal Audit.

Stakeholder Satisfaction

  • Achieve 90% stakeholder satisfaction across business units, Cyber Security, Audit, Compliance, Engineering, and Helpdesk through effective communication, roadmap transparency, and successful delivery of identity initiatives.

Identity Automation & Adoption

  • Increase adoption of Okta identity capabilities by delivering growth in SSO-enabled applications, automated provisioning & deprovisioning, and reduction of manual identity administration activities, as measure against ServiceNOW metrics and annual program targets.

title: Privacy Manager
description:
Job Description

Jeppesen Foreflight is one of the largest software development companies in Gothenburg. We develop and implement advanced Crew and Operations Management solutions used by several of the world’s leading airlines. From smarter crew scheduling to better aircraft utilization, our software systems make a real impact on global travel.

At Jeppesen’s office in central Gothenburg you will work in a one-of-a-kind software development organization with solutions that make a real difference to people around the world. You will be working in an agile learning organization, surrounded by a team of talented, creative and dedicated colleagues. You will learn and broaden your perspective by working with 400 professionals from more than 50 different nations but also be part of a global organization allowing for collaboration with customers and colleagues across the world. Most importantly, you will be expected to make a difference.

Role summary


The Privacy Manager supports the Data Protection Officer in the day-to-day operation of Jeppesen ForeFlight’s global privacy program. The role handles routine privacy assessments and requests, and is a key operational contact for the business, so that new processing activities, vendors and customer commitments are assessed and documented in line with the JFF Privacy Framework.

Key responsibilities

  • Carry out Privacy by Design reviews and vendor and integration assessments, escalating complex or high-risk matters to the DPO.
  • Handle data subject requests and customer privacy inquiries.
  • Maintain the record of processing activities and other privacy documentation.
  • Support personal data breach assessment.
  • Support the review of customer and vendor data processing agreements.
  • Contribute to the implementation of the Privacy Framework and the delivery of privacy training and awareness.

title: Space Composite Structure Engineer
description:
About GalaxEye

GalaxEye is building the world’s first OptoSAR LEO Earth observation satellites that combine multispectral optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging on a single platform, delivering all-weather, day-and-night imagery to governments, infrastructure enterprises, and geospatial analytics companies. We design our payloads and satellites in-house, from telescope to bus.

The role

You’ll own the composite structures that keep our electro-optical payloads stable in orbit: telescope structures, optical benches, baffles, and payload-to-bus interfaces, along with composite elements of the satellite structure. In an optical payload, a few microns of thermal distortion can ruin image quality, so your work directly determines what our satellites can see. You’ll take parts from concept through analysis, manufacturing with our vendors, and qualification testing.

Responsibilities:

  1. Design composite structures (CFRP laminates, sandwich panels, tubes, bonded joints, inserts) for optical payloads and spacecraft, with dimensional and thermo-elastic stability as primary drivers
  2. Define laminate layups, materials, and processes to meet stiffness, strength, CTE, mass, and outgassing requirements
  3. Perform structural and thermo-elastic analysis (static, modal, random vibration, sine, shock, thermal distortion) and work with the optical and thermal teams to close the structural-thermal-optical loop
  4. Manage manufacturing with composites vendors: tooling, layup, cure, machining, bonding, and inspection, including NDT
  5. Plan and support qualification and acceptance testing (vibration, shock, thermal vacuum, thermal cycling) and correlate analysis to test results
  6. Write design documentation, manufacturing and inspection procedures, and analysis reports for design reviews


Requirements

Skills/Requirements:
  1. B.E./B.Tech/M.Tech/MS in Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent
  2. 5–8 years designing and analysing composite structures, ideally for space, aerospace, or defence hardware
  3. Strong grasp of laminate theory, composite failure criteria, and design of bonded joints and inserts
  4. Hands-on experience with FEA tools (e.g. NASTRAN/Patran, Ansys ACP, HyperMesh, Abaqus) and CAD
  5. Experience taking composite parts through manufacturing, not just design and analysis
  6. Familiarity with space environment requirements: outgassing (ASTM E595), moisture effects on dimensional stability, and thermal cycling
  7. Proven history of managing complex, interdisciplinary manufacturing processes

Nice to have

  • Experience in building composite structures for optical instruments or other high-stability applications
  • Experience with high-modulus fibres (e.g. M55J) and near-zero-CTE layups
  • Exposure to ECSS or NASA structural standards and qualification test campaigns
  • Background with ISRO programmes or Indian space-qualified vendors


Benefits

  • Fair compensation will be provided as per market standards
  • Experience rapid growth and start-up culture
  • Flexible Working Hours
  • Open to exploring, discussing and implementing new ideas and processes
  • Opportunity to work closely with the Founding Team at GalaxEye
  • Get a chance to work with Advisors holding senior positions and decades of experience

title: Conventional EDM Operator
description:
Position Summary:

  • A Conventional EDM Operator shall operate Conventional EDM machines to machine production and complex tooling workpieces to specifications. A Conventional EDM Operator shall report to the Plant Manager and Conventional EDM Manager.

Responsibilities:

  • Set up and operate sinker EDM machines with precision to produce complex metal parts according to detailed specifications.
  • Adjust machine parameters and tooling setups to optimize cutting performance and ensure adherence to quality standards.
  • Inspect finished components using a precision CMM, measuring devices, and visual checks to verify dimensional accuracy.
  • Maintain and troubleshoot EDM equipment, ensuring optimal operation and minimal downtime.
  • Collaborate with the manufacturing team to plan production schedules, prioritize tasks, and meet delivery deadlines.
  • Assist in the development and modification of tooling fixtures for improved machining efficiency.
  • Follow safety protocols rigorously, including proper handling of power tools, hand tools, and warehouse equipment such as forklifts.

To perform this job successfully, the individual must be able to perform each essential function satisfactorily. The essential functions listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

A Conventional EDM Operator shall meet the following qualifications:

  • 1+ years of trade school, vocational education, work experience, apprenticeship, or equivalent

Physical Demands & Working Environment Summary:

  • Physical Activity:
    • Frequent to Constant (>2/3 of time): Standing, using hands to handle/finger/touch, and working near moving mechanical parts.
    • Moderate (1/3 to 2/3 of time): Walking, talking/hearing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, crawling, and experiencing vibration or risk of electrical shock.
    • Occasional (<1/3 of time): Sitting, using feet to operate controls, climbing/balancing, reaching above shoulders, and limited exposure to wet conditions, fumes, toxic chemicals, or precarious heights.
    • None: Tasting/smelling, outdoor weather, extreme hot/cold, explosives, or radiation.
  • Lifting & Exertion:
    • Routinely lifts and exerts force up to 25–50 pounds (up to 2/3 of the time). Does not lift over 50 pounds.
  • Vision Requirements:
    • Close vision (20 inches or less), color vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
  • Tools & Equipment:
    • Regularly operates Conventional EDM machines (>2/3 of time) and utilizes various inspection media (1/3 to 2/3 of time).
  • Noise Level: Moderate.

title: Sr Project Manager, Implementations

Jeppesen ForeFlight is seeking a Senior Project Manager, Implementations reporting to the Senior Manager, Professional Services Implementation & Deployment, to lead complex, customer-facing implementation and migration projects across our legacy and next-generation flight planning products, including our JetPlan Engine platform migration program moving customers off unsupported legacy hardware and operating systems onto current, supported infrastructure.

As a Senior Project Manager, you will own the end-to-end planning, scheduling, and delivery of multi-workstream implementation and migration projects, coordinating across Development, Deployment Specialists, Quality Assurance, and the customer's own technical team to move complex, production flight-planning systems safely from legacy infrastructure onto our current platforms.

A successful candidate is comfortable being the connective tissue across engineering, deployment, and the customer on a technically complex, high-stakes project, tracking schedule, risk, and dependencies with equal rigor. You're equally comfortable running a detailed cutover plan, presenting a clear status update to executive stakeholders, and keeping several concurrent migrations on track at once. You either know legacy-to-modern infrastructure migrations already, or you're eager to learn the space quickly.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own project planning, scheduling, and status reporting for one or more complex implementation and migration projects, from kickoff through go-live and into early production support handoff
  • Build and maintain detailed project plans, RAID logs (risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies), and cutover/go-live runbooks for each migration
  • Coordinate across Development, Deployment Specialists, Quality Assurance, and Support to sequence and de-risk cutover activities for production systems that cannot tolerate extended downtime
  • Manage and track project status in Salesforce, keeping stakeholders and leadership current on schedule, risk, and blockers
  • Lead recurring customer- and internal-facing status meetings, translating technical migration details into clear, actionable updates for both technical and executive stakeholders
  • Coordinate go-live/cutover events directly with customer technical teams, including scheduling maintenance windows and validating post-cutover system health
  • Identify and escalate schedule, resource, or technical risks early, and drive mitigation plans to closure
  • Support post-go-live stabilization and a clean handoff to ongoing support
  • Partner with Product, Support, and other internal teams to resolve issues and escalations surfaced during a migration
  • Travel to customer sites on occasion, as needed

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of project management experience delivering complex, technical implementation or migration projects, ideally including production system cutovers
  • Experience managing multi-stakeholder projects spanning internal engineering/deployment teams and external customer technical teams
  • Strong technical aptitude, comfortable understanding infrastructure migration concepts (e.g., legacy operating system to Linux platform migrations) well enough to plan and sequence around them, without requiring a software engineering background
  • Experience with Salesforce or a comparable CRM/project-tracking tool
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, comfortable presenting project status to both technical teams and executive stakeholders
  • Strong critical thinking and risk-management skills, with the ability to identify and mitigate schedule and technical risk before it becomes a problem
  • Willingness to learn and apply AI-powered tools to accelerate project tracking, status reporting, and cross-team coordination; prior hands-on experience with AI tools is a plus
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and prioritize independently

Preferred Qualifications:

  • PMP or a comparable project management certification
  • Experience in airline operations, flight dispatch, or aviation technology
  • Experience coordinating international, multi-time-zone customer implementations
  • Background in client or account management, with the ability to translate customer needs into a project plan
  • Comfort working across time zones with international customers

About Jeppesen ForeFlight:

Jeppesen ForeFlight is a leading provider of innovative aviation software solutions, serving the Commercial, Business, Military, and General Aviation sectors globally. Combining Jeppesen’s 90-year legacy of accurate aeronautical data with ForeFlight’s expertise in cutting-edge aviation technology, the company delivers an integrated suite of tools designed to enhance safety, improve operational efficiency, and sharpen decision-making.

Overview
The Inventory Control Manager is responsible for managing and controlling the processes and procedures that affect the quantity, quality, and accuracy of product inventory at a Chadwell Supply distribution facility. The Inventory Control Manager performs and oversees the daily cycle counts of products, procedures related to customer warranties, customer and vendor returns and prepares for and oversees the annual physical inventory. He/she also researches product quantity discrepancies and works with the Branch Manager to effect changes as required in processes, procedures, or Inventory Control staff. In addition, he/she participates in the recruiting, hiring, and training of new employees and approves timecards, administers performance reviews, and applies disciplinary measures as appropriate, all while coaching and developing their employees to be successful at Chadwell Supply.

What you will need
  • Be a minimum of 25 years of age.
  • Pass all pre-employment, background check, and drug testing.
  • Have previous employee supervision experience and a minimum of 3 years’ experience in a warehouse working environment.
  • Be fluent in reading, writing, understanding and communicating in English.
  • Basic literacy skills and excellent computer skills are required for this position.
  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • Must have working knowledge of ERP systems and warehouse operations.
  • Must have prior experience with cycle counting.
  • This position requires an ability to learn and adapt to changes in work processes.
How you will make an Impact
  • Strive to provide excellent customer service satisfaction through prompt and accurate product checking, counting, and stocking, along with communication with company personnel. • Product receiving, checking, counting, and stocking.
  • Oversee down stocking from overstock of any products to ensure that warehouse picking locations are filled to enable order pulling efficiency and accuracy.
  • Ensure that all stocked products are accurately recorded by bin location and quantity in the computer system.
  • Oversee Inventory Control department staff in receiving and ensuring that all inbound products from vendors and Distribution Centers are checked and counted against packing slips and review receiving documents for quantity and shipment accuracy.
  • Ensure that all products are stocked and shelved in the correct bin locations and that all product bin locations are changed as required for proper bin management and space allocation, and that the quantity in the computer system is correct.
  • Oversee the daily inspection of all warehouse product aisles and areas and receive written notification of any unsafe conditions.
  • Oversee or perform daily cycle counting, and processing of customer returns, warranties, and vendor returns.
  • Verify that all cycle counts performed by Inventory Control are completed promptly and accurately.
  • Assist in keeping the warehouse clean and safe
  • Research and resolve inventory discrepancies while overseeing the return process to ensure accuracy, efficiency, and timely resolution of issues.
What will set you apart:
  • Strong knowledge of warehouse operations
  • Ability to effectively lead and manage a team of 5–15 employees

title: Senior Case Manager
description:
The Senior Case Manager possesses extensive knowledge and understanding of personal injury. They assist attorneys with claim handling and negotiations, maintain contact with clients, and provide them with updates on case status.

Essential Functions:

Client Communication

  • Contact clients within 24 hours of receiving their case to introduce themselves.
  • Present initial settlement offers to clients within 48 hours of receipt.
  • Educate clients about further medical treatments such as injections, rhizotomies, surgeries, TBI treatment, etc.
  • Inform clients about the necessity to file lawsuits.
  • Return all client calls the same day.
  • Maintain bi-weekly communication with clients to ensure effective communication.
  • Inform clients of case settlements and explain the reductions process.

Insurance Communication

  • Follow up with insurance companies within 10 days after a settlement demand is sent and continue timely follow-ups until a response is received.
  • Communicate settlement offers and counteroffers under the direct supervision of an attorney.
  • Conduct settlement negotiations under the direct supervision of an attorney.
  • Confirm coverage information (UM, PIP, and BI coverages).
  • Follow up on Declaration pages from PIP, BI, UM, and UM Rejection forms if applicable.
  • Send UM subrogation waivers and follow up to confirm UM subrogation is waived.
  • Schedule mediations.
  • Prepare mediation/global settlement/settlement conference summaries or presentations.

File Notation

  • Log initial offers within 24 hours of receipt.
  • Maintain thorough and accurate notes/records in Litify.
  • Keep client files updated in Litify.
  • Track offers, demands, and client authority in the negotiation link.
  • Save documents or photos in the appropriate folder.
  • Enter case resolution details in the resolution link.
  • Pay outstanding invoices and keep the expenses link updated.
  • Review and update links for injuries and treatment, approval requests, liens, Litify notes, litigations, negotiations, requests, resolutions, etc.
  • Use appropriate call subjects when logging calls.

Case Review

  • Review settlement offers before sending them to insurance companies.
  • Revise surgical case reviews before clients undergo procedures.
  • Conduct weekly audits for all cases.
  • Discharge cases as needed.
  • Draft and file lawsuits on behalf of the attorney, when applicable.
  • Dismiss lawsuits on behalf of the attorney, when applicable.

Provider Communication

  • Obtain estimates from providers before closing cases.
  • Follow up and obtain health insurance liens.
  • Check provider balances and obtain POD leader authority before settling cases with hospitals.

Client Service

  • Ensure high standards of client service and satisfaction.
  • Address client concerns and inquiries promptly and professionally.
  • Contact clients every 14 days.
  • Return client voicemails the same day.

Required Skills/Abilities:

  • Strong organizational and leadership skills.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities.
  • Proficiency in Litify software and Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Must be fluent in English and Spanish.
  • Must consistently be on time and reliable.
  • Must work well in a team environment.
  • Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to successfully communicate with other employees.

Education and Experience:

  • Prior case-management/personal-injury experience preferred.

Physical Requirements:

  • Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times.
  • Must be able to access and navigate each department at the organization’s facilities.

Caseload & Performance Requirements

  • Possess expert knowledge and understanding of the complete Bodily Injury Claims process.
  • Manage an average caseload of 80–120 Personal Injury cases.
  • Achieve a minimum settlements target of per month.
  • Meet a minimum requirement of 3 surgeries, 5 rhizotomies, and 5 injections per month for additional treatments.
  • Review all settlement offers, additional demands, and surgery reviews within 48 hours of receipt.

Additional Training Requirements

  • Required to attend additional in-person training, which may occasionally be scheduled on weekends, including Saturdays and Sundays. Employees will be given 30-day notice prior to scheduled training to make arrangements to attend in person.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Technical Requirements

Contractors supply their own equipment and workspace. Your setup must meet these minimums:

Computer — capable of running a browser-based ATS, video conferencing, and a softphone simultaneously without degradation:

  • Windows: Windows 11, Intel i5 (8th generation or newer) or equivalent, 16 GB RAM, 256 GB SSD
  • Mac: macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer, Apple Silicon or Intel i5, 16 GB RAM, 256 GB SSD
  • The device must be used solely by you — not shared with family or household members

Internet — wired Ethernet preferred, 5 GHz Wi-Fi acceptable:

  • 30 Mbps download / 15 Mbps upload minimum
  • Latency under 100 ms
  • Private, password-protected network. Public Wi-Fi is not permitted for this work.

Peripherals:

  • USB noise-cancelling headset with microphone
  • Webcam capable of clear video for scheduled calls

Security — required for handling confidential applicant information:

  • Full-disk encryption enabled (BitLocker or FileVault)
  • Automatic security updates enabled for operating system and browser
  • Screen lock after no more than 10 minutes idle
  • Active endpoint protection software
  • Applicant data stored only in firm-designated systems — never on personal cloud storage or local drives

Additional Information

Contractor Terms

  • This is an independent contractor engagement, not employment.
  • No paid time off, healthcare, retirement, or other employee benefits are provided.
  • You will supply your own equipment, software, internet connection, and workspace.
